source.title: CritICL: Inference-Time Weak-to-Strong Generalization from Small Language Model Failure Modes
source.authors: Yu-Fan Wu; Ying-Hui He; Zhengyi Hu; Lang Wei; Rui-Chen Li; Qi-Fan Yang; Ting Zhu

page_placements.theme: In-context weak-to-strong: weak-labelled examples, critiques of weak errors or a weaker expert's insights given as demonstrations

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports weak-to-strong transfer in a distinct inference-time setting: weak-model failure information is retrieved as in-context critique examples for stronger models. It does not test the original fine-tuning intervention or PGR.
record.gate_note: CritICL uses failure modes and critiques derived from weaker models to guide stronger models at inference time, and reports accuracy outcomes. The paper explicitly says it does not fine-tune the target model. It does not calculate PGR or compare the weak supervisor with a strong model trained on true labels. Consequently, the reported outcomes concern an inference-time extension, not the listed training-time claim versions. The results of other baselines are recorded only where needed as references for CritICL rows.
record.test_reason: CritICL injects retrieved critiques of weak-model errors into a strong model's prompt at inference time. No strong model is trained on weak labels, and no weak-supervisor or ceiling comparison or PGR is reported. The critiques and failure labels come from gpt-4o-mini, a frontier model, so the guidance is not purely weak supervision. The paper borrows the W2SG name and contrasts itself with Burns et al. but tests none of V1–V6. The reader's 'tests'/T3 contradicts its own finding that every version is not_tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Also note that the authors attribute the transfer to shared within-family failure distributions. They also concede that differences against the best baseline on AMC23 and AIME are not significant.
record.recipe_differences: CritICL retrieves weak-model error examples, labels, and critiques into inference prompts; it does not fine-tune a strong student on weak labels or calculate PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with target model, benchmark, CritICL variant, and whether the CritBank comes from the same or another model family. The paper reports stronger transfer within families than across families.

fits_no_version.finding: Prompting strong instruct models with critiques of weak same-family models' errors raises accuracy over 5-shot ICL. Examples: Qwen2.5-72B MATH 80.5 to 84.0; Llama-3.1-70B GPQA avg 68.6 to 74.4. Gains are smaller with cross-family CritBanks, and most differences against the best baseline are non-significant (Table 9).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weak-model failure critiques, written by a frontier model, improve stronger models' reasoning as in-context examples, more so within a model family.

fits_no_version.finding: Failure-mode distributions of weak and strong same-family models are highly similar. Aggregate profiles reach Spearman 0.91 for Qwen and 0.88 for Llama, versus about 0.45 across families (Table 4, Fig. 2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weak and strong models in the same family share error-type distributions, an error-similarity measure relevant to but distinct from V4's shared-error effect on PGR.

record.problems: The study does not test training-time weak supervision, compare against a weak supervisor or strong true-label ceiling, or report PGR. Main comparisons are inference-time prompting methods. The text reports bootstrap uncertainty and significance tests for selected Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct comparisons; AIME evaluation sets are described as small, with wide confidence intervals.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted separately reported aggregate accuracy columns from Tables 1 and 12 (ID/OOD averages and overall averages), additional inference-cost measurements in Tables 2, 13–15, retrieval-selection ablations in Table 3, source-of-gain ablations in Table 7, and cross-domain transfer results in Table 11. These are inference-time method or cost analyses and do not measure the listed training-time claim versions.

untested.parts: No fine-tuning on weak labels, weak-supervisor baseline, strong ceiling or PGR.
No training-time method changes. Retrieval variants are prompting methods.
No PGR versus supervisor or student size, and no PGR versus task.
No exploitation, distribution-shift PGR, or PGR versus error similarity. Shared failure-mode similarity is measured but not linked to PGR.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts are given because no version is tested. The method's critiques are produced by gpt-4o-mini, so 'weak-to-strong' here is not weak supervision in the Burns sense. Bootstrap tests cover only Qwen2.5-72B CritICL-static against the best baseline. MATH is significant (p=0.018) and the macro average is significant (p=0.041); GSM8K, AMC23 and AIME are not.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on weak-model labels, weak-supervisor comparison, strong true-label ceiling, or PGR.
No training changes to fine-tuning on weak labels are tested; retrieval variants are inference-time methods.
No PGR analysis, supervisor/student size sweep for PGR, representation predictor analysis, or training-time task comparison.
No test of students exploiting supervisor blind spots, PGR under distribution shift, or shared-error effects on PGR.
No theoretical conditions for a student to beat its supervisor are derived or tested.

relation.reason: Appendix A discusses conventional weak-to-strong generalization and explicitly distinguishes CritICL's inference-time guidance from training on weak labels or preferences.

tranche.reason: CritICL measures inference-time improvement from retrieved critiques, without fine-tuning on weak labels, comparing students with weak supervisors and strong ceilings, or reporting PGR. Its results do not test a listed claim version.

source_check.notes: Failure labels and critiques are generated by gpt-4o-mini; weak models supply incorrect responses. Table 9 p-values compare CritICL-static with the strongest baseline, not the rows' fixed 5-shot baseline.
